summary: A [third national development plan was adopted by decree on 30 June 2026](2026-06-30-conseil-ministres-pnd-adeeg-2025-2030-adoption-adi), after a period with no adopted successor plan.
developments:
There was no adopted successor plan at the window's opening. 2026-06-30 - the [2025-2030 plan was adopted by decree in the Council of Ministers](2026-06-30-conseil-ministres-pnd-adeeg-2025-2030-adoption-adi).

The plan text is not held, so its digital content, costing and delivery arrangements are not established from anything on file. The standing frame above it is [Vision 2035, in force at both ends of the window and restated at a Geneva summit in July 2026 as the basis of the digital-hub ambition](2026-07-09-geneva-wsis-djibouti-digital-hub-vision-lanation).

summary: The [first national artificial-intelligence strategy is complete and set to launch at a forum on 2 and 3 September 2026](2026-08-13-djibouti-ai-forum-sovereignty-snia-strategy).
developments:
None existed at the window's opening; [development began with United Nations support](2026-01-29 Djibouti develops national AI strategy with UN support), and [support was sought from the telecommunications union and a continental body](2026-07-13 Djibouti Seeks ITU, Smart Africa Support for Telecoms and AI Development).

The strategy is now [complete and set for official launch at the country's first national artificial-intelligence forum, dated 2 and 3 September 2026 at Djibouti-Ville](2026-08-13-djibouti-ai-forum-sovereignty-snia-strategy), the ministry [announcing an artificial-intelligence village at the Palais du Peuple framed around domestic developers and researchers](2026-08-20-intelligence-artificielle-jeunesse-djibouti) and [interministerial coordination for it](2026-08-15-djibouti-ai-forum-interministerial-coordination).

The text is still not held, so the launch date is the only new fact and the content remains unpublished.

summary: The [data-protection regime sits inside the Digital Code at 156 articles](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law), with none of its obligations evidenced in operation.
developments:
The regime is [in force within the Digital Code across 156 articles, providing for seventy-two-hour breach notification, mandatory data-protection officers and a public register](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law), and [none is evidenced in operation](2025-07-01 Djibouti Digital Code adopted by National Assembly).

Alongside it a [tiered prior-authorisation regime for national-identifier and biometric processing is in force, with no authorisation on record for the police body-camera fleet](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law). Nothing amended either in the window: what changed is what is being processed under them, not the law.

summary: [No artificial-intelligence law, decree or procurement rule is held](2026-01-29-national-ai-strategy-wearetech); the strategy in preparation is not an instrument.
developments:
The position is unchanged at both ends of the window: [no law, decree or procurement rule governing artificial-intelligence systems in public use is held](2026-01-29-national-ai-strategy-wearetech), and the strategy under preparation is not an instrument.

It matters more here than the absence alone suggests, because systems are already in public use: a weather early-warning system in service and a memorandum for a compute zone signed. Nothing published states what a public body must do before deploying such a system, who may audit it, or what a person subject to one may contest.

summary: The [Digital Code, eight volumes and about 800 articles adopted on 30 June 2025, is in force with no implementing decree held](2025-07-02-digital-code-enacted-techafricanews).
developments:
The code was [adopted by the National Assembly on 30 June 2025](2025-07-01 Djibouti Digital Code adopted by National Assembly), three weeks before the window opened, and is [in force across eight volumes and about 800 articles](2025-07-02-digital-code-enacted-techafricanews), [explained at length in the state daily](2025-07-13-code-du-numerique-digital-code-explainer-lanation).

No implementing decree is held for any of its volumes. It is the instrument on which the data-protection regime, the prior-authorisation regime and the supervisory commission all rest, and none of the three is evidenced in operation - so a code of eight hundred articles has produced no secondary instrument the base can show in the thirteen months since.

summary: The [supervisory commission established by the Digital Code has no record of its constitution, membership, register or decisions](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law).
developments:
The commission is [established by the Digital Code, and the base holds no record of its constitution, membership, register or decisions](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law) at either end of the window.

Thirteen months after a code of about eight hundred articles took effect, the body that would enforce its data-protection volume cannot be shown to exist. The public register of processing the same code provides for is therefore also unevidenced, and the prior-authorisation regime has no authority on record to grant an authorisation.

summary: [Body-worn cameras are in routine police use](2026-08-04-djibouti-bodycam-police-nationale) with no retention period, access rule, data controller or authorising instrument published.
developments:
The cameras were not on record at the window's opening. They are now [described as standard issue for the national police and road-safety officers, in routine use in central Djibouti with visible wearing and notification protocols and manual or automatic triggers](2026-08-04-djibouti-bodycam-police-nationale). The account is the state daily's and is framed as reassurance.

No [retention period, access rule, data controller or authorising instrument is published](2026-08-04-djibouti-bodycam-police-nationale), and no prior authorisation for the fleet is on record under the regime the Digital Code requires for biometric processing. A biometric-capable surveillance capability entering routine use while its supervisor cannot be shown to exist is the readiness position.

summary: The country [signed the United Nations cybercrime convention in Hanoi in October 2025](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority), having ratified the continental convention in 2023.
developments:
The [continental convention on cyber security and personal data protection was ratified in November 2023 and is unchanged](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority).

2025-10 - the country [signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime in Hanoi as one of seventy-one signatories](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority); no ratification instrument is on file.

Both are ratified or signed by a state whose own data-protection supervisor is unevidenced, so the harmonisation is at treaty level and has no domestic enforcement body the base can point to.

summary: The digital agency's [2026 budget was approved at 396,120,056 FDJ, down from 556.7m the year before](2025-12-30-djibouti-conseil-des-ministres-30-decembre-2025).
developments:
No domestic digital appropriation was held at the window's opening. 2025-12-30 - the agency's [2026 budget was approved at 396,120,056 FDJ, down from 556.7m FDJ in 2025, with investment of 108.1m FDJ for application firewalls, an archiving system, datacentre colocation and support renewal on the data-exchange layer, the balance largely staff costs](2025-12-30-djibouti-conseil-des-ministres-30-decembre-2025).

That is the agency's whole operating budget rather than a purpose-matched digital line, and the digital-specific component is the investment figure. No separate ministry line or e-government envelope is published, and the [budget law itself carries digital obligations without appropriating against them](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026). The arrete is not published, so a Council of Ministers record is the strongest evidence reached.

summary: A [startup fund of funds is provided for in the Startup Act](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act), with no implementing decree and no capital committed.
developments:
The fund did not exist at the window's opening. It is now [provided for at articles 25 to 28 of the Startup Act, with the management company to be tendered, no implementing decree and no capital committed](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act).

It is the only instrument on this ledger addressed to mobilising non-state money for digital ventures, and it stands where the whole Act stands: in force, with every operative detail deferred to decrees that have not been made.

summary: Three lender commitments stand with [no implementation report held](2025-01-01-wb-dji-001-djibouti-economic-and-financial-governance-project) for any of them.
developments:
A [US$20,000,000 economic and financial governance project is committed with no implementation report held](2025-01-01-wb-dji-001-djibouti-economic-and-financial-governance-project), and [US$11,422,000 for higher-education digitalisation likewise](2020-01-01-afd-dji-001-djibouti-digitalisation-and-professionalisation-of-higher). Both are year-precise and stated in dollars by the financier.

Submarine cable financing runs to [US$55.7m across two projects, US$16,844,185 in 2015 and US$38,830,000 in 2019, with no disbursement record held](2019-01-01-isdb-dji-dare-submarine-cable-2019-dare-regional-submarine-cable-project), the [earlier one a regional submarine telecommunications project](2015-01-01-isdb-dji-submarine-telecom-2015-regional-submarine-telecommunications-project).

Nothing moved on any of the three in the window, and no recipient-side account of any of them is on file.

summary: The incumbent's [statutory monopoly stands under two laws, with no competing licensed operator](2026-01-22-djibouti-telecom-monopoly-profile-lanation).
developments:
The [monopoly is restated in the operator's own profile and no competing licensed operator exists](2026-01-22-djibouti-telecom-monopoly-profile-lanation), unchanged at both ends of the window. The profile's cable and capacity figures are stale and are not carried here.

No subscriber count, penetration rate, coverage figure or tariff is published by the operator or by any regulator, for any date in the window. A country carrying a substantial share of the world's submarine cable traffic publishes no measure of how many of its own people are connected.

summary: A [binding agreement for a 2,800 km terrestrial corridor to Addis Ababa and Port Sudan was signed on 4 February 2026](2026-02-05-horizon-fiber-djibouti-ethio-sudatel-lanation), from a memorandum only.
developments:
The corridor stood at a [memorandum of understanding in December 2024](2026-02-04-horizon-fiber-tripartite-deal-techafricanews). 2026-02-04 - a [binding agreement was signed in Djibouti covering about 2,800 km, 144 fibre pairs and about 14 ms latency](2026-02-05-horizon-fiber-djibouti-ethio-sudatel-lanation), [reported across the trade press](2026-02-06-horizon-fiber-corridor-deal-itweb). No service date is published, and the route and latency figures are the three operators' own.

Domestically, the fibre programme moved from the [Ali-Sabieh regional hospital connected and over 200 km deployed in June 2025](2025-06-25-dfn-ali-sabieh-regional-hospital-fibre-lanation) to [a school, sub-prefecture and clinic at Damerjog connected in October 2025](2025-10-22-dfn-damerjog-school-subprefecture-fibre-lanation), with a [stakeholder and grievance workshop covering the capital, Balbala and the five interior regions](2025-07-30-dfn-eardip-stakeholder-grievance-workshop-lanation).

summary: [Twelve submarine systems land in the country, carrying about 18% of international submarine cable data](2026-08-03-il-ministro-bernini-a-gibuti-e-il-progetto-med-or-sull-underwater), and a southern extension is under build.
developments:
[Twelve operational systems were reached by the two carrier-neutral facilities in June 2025](2025-06-06-wingu-60m-east-africa-expansion-connectingafrica), and [twelve now land, six of them connected to Italy, carrying about 18% of international submarine cable data](2026-08-03-il-ministro-bernini-a-gibuti-e-il-progetto-med-or-sull-underwater). Both counts are the reporting parties' own; no landing register is held.

2025-09 - a [southern extension of the regional cable was announced at 36 Tbit/s over about 3,200 to 3,500 km, ready for service in 2028](2025-09-01-dare1-extension-techafricanews), [reported across three outlets](2025-09-01-dare1-extension-kenya-south-africa-connectingafrica).

2026-08-03 - an [Italian cable inspection and protection project at the landing station was reported during a ministerial mission, under a memorandum with the finance ministry and with no amount, term or delivery date](2026-08-03-il-ministro-bernini-a-gibuti-e-il-progetto-med-or-sull-underwater).

summary: [Two exchange points operate](2025-06-06-wingu-60m-east-africa-expansion-connectingafrica), a national one and an international operator's, both unchanged in the window.
developments:
The [two exchanges are in operation, a national point and one run by an international exchange operator alongside it](2025-06-06-wingu-60m-east-africa-expansion-connectingafrica), the second [launched with a carrier-neutral facility expansion](2025-06-05-wingu-60m-rmb-funding-biometricupdate).

Nothing moved in the window. No traffic figure, member count or peering policy is published for either, so what they carry is unknown - which is the same gap that sits under the country's whole transit position, where the landing count is published and the capacity is not.

summary: The incumbent's chief executive [states there is no clear regulatory framework for new entrants](2025-04-03-djibouti-telecom-at-a-crossroads); no licensing decision is on file.
developments:
The position is unchanged at both ends: the [incumbent's chief executive states there is no clear regulatory framework for new entrants, and no licensing decision is on file](2025-04-03-djibouti-telecom-at-a-crossroads).

It is a cited absence rather than an unexamined one, and it is stated by the party the absence protects. No application, refusal, consultation or draft framework for satellite market entry appears anywhere on this ledger, in a country whose interior regions the domestic fibre programme is still reaching one facility at a time.

summary: The [Tier III facility and cable landing station inaugurated in November 2024 is in service](2024-11-25 Djibouti inaugurates Wingu TO7 Tier-3 data centre and cable landing station); a second joint venture has not moved.
developments:
The facility was [inaugurated on 25 November 2024 and is in service](2024-11-25 Djibouti inaugurates Wingu TO7 Tier-3 data centre and cable landing station), unchanged through the window, with no capacity, utilisation or tenant figure published.

A [data centre joint venture between an operator and the sovereign fund was announced with no construction on record, and its stated first phase of 2026 is unverified; the 50,000 square feet, 5 MW and US$50m figures are the parties' own](2024-05-15 PAIX-Djibouti Sovereign Fund data centre joint venture (JIB1)). Nothing on file since the announcement.

summary: A [US$1.35bn memorandum for an artificial-intelligence compute centre and special economic zone was signed on 19 July 2026](2026-07-19-linkwise-group-dji-2026-record), valid one year.
developments:
The project did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-07-19 - a [US$1.35bn memorandum of understanding was signed, valid one year, with no investment protocol, no disbursement and no site](2026-07-19-linkwise-group-dji-2026-record), [set out by the signing minister](2026-07-23-lanation-djibouti-linkwise-interview-mariam-hamadou-ali) and [presented as an innovation-pole partnership](2026-07-23-lanation-partenariat-linkwise-pole-innovation).

The stated 100 MW capacity is the promoters' own, and no feasibility study or site is on file. It is by an order of magnitude the largest figure on this ledger, and it is a one-year memorandum.

summary: [Up to 500 MW of solar, wind and storage is provided for in the compute-zone memorandum](2026-07-19-linkwise-group-dji-2026-record); nothing is contracted or built.
developments:
No generation for digital infrastructure was on record at the window's opening. The memorandum [provides for up to 500 MW of solar, wind and storage, with nothing contracted or built](2026-07-19-linkwise-group-dji-2026-record), the figure being the promoters' own and [restated in the signing minister's account](2026-07-23-lanation-djibouti-linkwise-interview-mariam-hamadou-ali).

It is the only energy statement attached to digital infrastructure in this country's record. No measured load, tariff, grid-connection arrangement or efficiency figure is published for the facilities already operating.

summary: A [statutory cyber authority became operational in December 2025](2025-12-09 Djibouti Launches National Cyber Security Authority (ANC operational, DG named)), and its response team [took part in a regional exercise](2026-07-09-anc-dj-cert-igad-cyber-exercise-lanation).
developments:
There was no statutory cyber authority at the window's opening, only a pre-statutory label and a directorate inside the digital agency. A [law carried in the official journal of 15 December 2025 created an autonomous public establishment under the Presidency](2025-12-15 Loi n 195-AN-25 portant creation de l'Autorite Nationale de Cybersecurite (Djibouti, JO)), [operational from December 2025 with a director-general named](2025-12-09 Djibouti Launches National Cyber Security Authority (ANC operational, DG named)), after the [bill advanced in November](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority).

2026-06-26 to 30 - its [incident response team took part in a regional exercise and is reported to have placed first in both simulation scenarios](2026-07-09-anc-dj-cert-igad-cyber-exercise-lanation); the placing is the state daily's and the organiser has published no result. The [2024-2030 five-pillar strategy is unchanged](2024-12-02 Djibouti National Cybersecurity Strategy 2024-2030).

summary: A [prices database and central-administration data-exchange platform was ordered by article 38 of the 2026 budget law](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026), with no design or date.
developments:
Neither existed at the window's opening. The [2026 budget law orders a prices database and a data-exchange platform on the budget execution directorate, to be established with every central-administration department as the counterpart to a central purchasing body created by the preceding article, with no design, delivery date, budget line or operating rule stated](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026).

2026-07 - [real-time identity verification for banks and social protection is named as in preparation by the population directorate, with no date published](2026-07-23-lanation-dgpf-administration-modernisee-interconnectee).

Both are ordered or announced rather than built, and the exchange layer the digital agency already runs support on is not stated to be what either would use.

summary: A [biometric national identity card has been issued nationwide since 2025](2026-07-23-lanation-carte-nationale-identite-biometrique), with mobile enrolment kits.
developments:
No biometric national identity card was on record at the window's opening. It is now [issued nationwide with mobile enrolment kits, capturing fingerprints, iris, photograph and electronic signature against a national identification number held in the register of natural persons](2026-07-23-lanation-carte-nationale-identite-biometrique), the [population directorate describing the register as the spine of a modernised and interconnected administration](2026-07-23-lanation-dgpf-administration-modernisee-interconnectee).

No enrolment total, coverage rate or issuance figure is published at any date, so how far nationwide reaches is unestablished - and the prior-authorisation regime the Digital Code sets for national-identifier and biometric processing has no supervisory body on record to have applied it.

summary: A [mobile digital identity platform entered service on 9 February 2026](2026-02-09-mobile-id-national-digital-identity-forum-lanation), carrying authentication and electronic signature.
developments:
The platform did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-02-09 - it was [launched at a national digital identity forum, in service for authentication and electronic signature, with biometric data held only by the Interior Ministry](2026-02-09-mobile-id-national-digital-identity-forum-lanation), [reported across the trade press](2026-02-10-mobile-id-launch-wearetech) and [in the biometrics press](2026-02-10-mobile-id-biometric-launch-biometricupdate).

Interoperability with driving-licence and health records is stated as planned rather than delivered. No activation count, service count or transaction figure has been published since launch, so what the credential is used for is unknown.

summary: The [state personnel file was ordered updated by article 32 of the 2026 budget law](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026) to integrate contract staff and unregularised headcounts.
developments:
The file existed and its position at the window's opening is not held. The [2026 budget law orders the budget ministry, jointly with the labour ministry charged with administrative reform, to update the database to integrate contract staff and headcounts awaiting regularisation, with no completion date, budget line or headcount stated](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026).

A payroll database that a finance law has to order updated to include the staff already being paid from it is the position as the base holds it. No count of records, no audit and no remediation report follows it on file.

summary: The [mobile wallet has been in service since June 2020](2023-12-11-lanation-djibouti-lancement-premiere-plateforme-paiement-en-ligne-d-money) and its online payment gateway since December 2023.
developments:
The wallet has been [in service since June 2020, with an online payment gateway launched under the Prime Minister's patronage on 10 December 2023](2023-12-11-lanation-djibouti-lancement-premiere-plateforme-paiement-en-ligne-d-money) and [extended to the ports](2023-12-12 Djibouti Telecom extends D-Money mobile payments to ports).

Neither moved in the window and no subscriber, wallet or transaction figure has ever been published for either. The conventions signed on the gateway's launch day are named by category only and are not held. Both are the incumbent's, in a market with no competing licensed operator.

summary: A [memorandum for a national digital wallet was signed on 16 September 2025](2025-09-19 Djibouti-Visa Smart Wallet national digital wallet MoU), targeting a 60% cut in cash use.
developments:
Nothing existed at the window's opening. 2025-09-16 - a [memorandum was signed with a card network and a biometrics supplier for a national digital wallet, with nothing in service and no rollout calendar](2025-09-19 Djibouti-Visa Smart Wallet national digital wallet MoU).

The stated target of a large cut in cash use within three years is the parties' own. No baseline cash-use figure, account count or transaction volume exists anywhere on this ledger to measure it against, and the wallet already in service publishes none either - so the country's payment uptake is stated only as an ambition.

summary: [Civil-registry archive digitisation is running alongside enrolment](2026-07-23-lanation-dgpf-administration-modernisee-interconnectee), with staffing and archive space named as the constraints.
developments:
The programme was not on record at the window's opening. It is [under way alongside biometric enrolment, with staffing and archive space named as the constraints and no completion date published](2026-07-23-lanation-dgpf-administration-modernisee-interconnectee).

No record count, coverage figure or registration rate is held at any date. The directorate that runs it is the same one preparing real-time identity verification for banks and social protection, so a register whose digitisation is constrained by staffing and shelf space is the intended source for those checks.

summary: An [online company creation platform was launched by the Prime Minister on 26 January 2026](2026-01-27-djibouti-online-company-creation-platform-lanation), completing formation without attendance.
developments:
The platform did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-01-26 - it was [launched by the Prime Minister and is in service, with company formation completed without attendance](2026-01-27-djibouti-online-company-creation-platform-lanation).

No registration count through the platform is published. The [company-creation and survival figures that accompany the announcement are the investment agency's own study and cover the one-stop counter rather than the platform](2026-01-27-djibouti-online-company-creation-platform-lanation), so nothing on file measures what the online route has actually done.

summary: [Inter-hospital medical record sharing runs at one connected hospital](2025-06-25-dfn-ali-sabieh-regional-hospital-fibre-lanation) and no further site is reported.
developments:
The service is [in operation at the Ali-Sabieh regional hospital over the national fibre network, and no further site is reported](2025-06-25-dfn-ali-sabieh-regional-hospital-fibre-lanation).

Nothing moved in the window. The before-and-after comparison is the hospital's own account, and no patient volume, record count, standard or governing instrument is published. It is the only health information system of any kind on this ledger, and it covers one hospital.

summary: The customs system was [constituted by statute as the single window, with the electronic route obligatory for all economic operators](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026).
developments:
The customs clearance system was [in service as a governance case study](2024-01-01 WB GovTech Case Study - Djibouti Digital Customs ASYCUDAWorld). The [2026 budget law constitutes it as the single window under the customs directorate, centralising the declaration, certificates of origin, licences, freight manifests, control results and sanitary and phytosanitary certificates; the electronic route is obligatory for all economic operators with paper admitted only by derogation on a duly established technical impossibility, duties and taxes are paid electronically, and the customs and treasury systems must be interconnected for daily and monthly reconciliation of collected revenue](2025-12-31-djibouti-loi-de-finances-203-an-25-budget-initial-2026).

The [port community system remains the mandatory national platform for import, export and transit data and was presented as a best-practice example at a regional seminar in April 2026](2026-04-29-dpcs-port-digitalisation-imo-worldbank-best-practice-lanation); no transaction volume is published for either.

summary: A [business platform entered design in December 2025](2025-12-18-g2b-platform-techafricanews), and the [state archive programme signed an accord in August 2026](2026-08-03-djibouti-sgg-pnud-dematerialisation-archives-etat).
developments:
2025-12-15 - a [design phase was launched for an integrated business platform on three pillars: a startups portal, a government-to-business counter and an extension of the one-stop counter](2025-12-18 Djibouti begins one-stop G2B digital platform for businesses), [reported the same week](2025-12-18-g2b-platform-techafricanews). Nothing is reported built.

The archive programme has run [state-funded since 2023 with over 200,000 secured digital files for the Presidency, and signed a letter of accord with the UN development programme on 2 August 2026 extending it to the audit and integrity institutions from September 2026](2026-08-03-djibouti-sgg-pnud-dematerialisation-archives-etat). The accord's text, value and duration are not stated, and delivery is asserted by the parties at signature rather than independently measured.

summary: A [weather early-warning system entered service in version 2.0](2026-07-22-djibouti-mazu-2-0-alerte-meteo-ia), forecasting at 3 km resolution against 9 km.
developments:
The first system was supplied in July 2025 and not yet in service. 2026-07 - [version 2.0 was handed over on the sidelines of a Shanghai conference and is in service, with forecast resolution of 3 km against 9 km, a three-day horizon and six-hourly updates](2026-07-22-djibouti-mazu-2-0-alerte-meteo-ia).

It is supplied by the Chinese meteorological administration throughout. No accuracy assessment, warning count or user figure is published, and it operates in a country where no instrument governs artificial-intelligence systems in public use - so an early-warning system on which safety decisions rest has no published audit route.

summary: A [cross-border data corridor is provided for in the compute memorandum](2026-07-23-lanation-djibouti-linkwise-interview-mariam-hamadou-ali), against a [readiness score of 24.5 out of 100](2026-08-13-djibouti-ai-forum-sovereignty-snia-strategy).
developments:
The corridor did not exist at the window's opening. It is [provided for in the compute memorandum and named by the signing minister as a success indicator, stated alongside full national jurisdiction over data generated on the territory, with nothing built](2026-07-23-lanation-djibouti-linkwise-interview-mariam-hamadou-ali); the memorandum text is not held.

The national readiness position is [an estimated 24.5 out of 100 on a diagnostic described as an emergent level, against an information and communication technology development index of 61.6 attributed to the submarine cables landing here and to the data centres](2026-08-13-djibouti-ai-forum-sovereignty-snia-strategy). The assessment report is not held and neither index's methodology is named, so the gap between the two scores is the finding rather than either number.

summary: A [national federation of digital enterprises was reported created in December 2025](2025-12-15-federation-nationale-entreprises-numerique-wearetech), with no constitution published.
developments:
The federation did not exist at the window's opening. Its [creation was reported in December 2025, as a founding member of a continental federation under a declaration signed at Marrakech, with no constitution or membership published](2025-12-15-federation-nationale-entreprises-numerique-wearetech).

Nothing since reports a member count, a statute, an office or an activity. It is the only industry body on this ledger, in a market where the sole telecommunications operator holds a statutory monopoly and no sector revenue, employment or firm-count figure is published by anyone.

summary: An [innovation platform was launched by the digital economy ministry in July 2026](2026-07-04-limo-ministry-platform-techreviewafrica), with no user or service figures.
developments:
The platform did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-07 - it was [launched by the Minister Delegate for the Digital Economy and Innovation, with no user or service figures published](2026-07-04-limo-ministry-platform-techreviewafrica).

The account is trade press reporting a ministry announcement, and the platform is distinct from a private marketplace of the same name. No incubator, accelerator or technology park appears anywhere else on this ledger, so a ministry-run platform with no published usage is the whole of the country's hub provision.

progress: Mixed, the Startup Act came into force in December 2025 while none of the decrees carrying its label, sandbox, visa or fund has been made
summary: The [Startup Act is in force from promulgation with every operative detail deferred to implementing decrees](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act), and [none is held](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act).
developments:
The Act did not exist at the window's opening. It was [signed on 1 December 2025 and carried in the official journal of 15 December, in force from promulgation with every operative detail deferred to implementing decrees](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act), after [advancing through November](2025-11-12-startup-act-advances-techafricanews) and being [reported across the trade press](2025-11-14-startup-act-djibouti-wearetech).

No decree is held as at 20 July 2026, so no label award, sandbox admission or visa issue can be stated. The [regulatory sandbox at articles 31 and 32](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act) and the [startup visa at article 15, a three-year renewable residence card with an automatic work permit](2026-01-08-djibouti-loi-179-an-25-startup-act) are provided for with no admission or issue on record.

summary: A [civil-service digital skills programme is running](2025-02-24-digital-skills-program-govt-officials-wearetech) with no completion figures published.
developments:
The programme was [launched with a domestic cloud operator, a vendor university and the national public administration institute and is running](2025-02-24-digital-skills-program-govt-officials-wearetech), unchanged at both ends of the window.

No completion figures, cohort sizes or curriculum are published. It predates the window's opening by five months and nothing since revises it, so a programme in progress with no measured output is the position - which matters because the administration it trains is the one now running biometric enrolment, a mobile identity credential and a statutory single window.

summary: A [coding school project was launched with European partners in April 2026](2026-04-06-ecole-42-djibouti-techreviewafrica), with no intake or opening date published.
developments:
The school did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-04 - a [project was launched with the European Union, a French technical agency and the school's own association, with no intake or opening date published](2026-04-06-ecole-42-djibouti-techreviewafrica).

It is a project rather than an institution: no site, curriculum, capacity or first cohort is on record. Against a national artificial-intelligence readiness score in the mid-twenties and a compute memorandum in the billions, the country's training provision is one announced school and one civil-service programme with no published output.

summary: [Digital houses were announced across five inland regions, 3,000 to be trained by 2029 at a stated EUR 7m](2026-05-16-digital-houses-e-skills-wearetech); no site is open.
developments:
The initiative did not exist at the window's opening. 2026-05 - it was [announced across five inland regions, with 3,000 to be trained by 2029 at a stated EUR 7m and no site open on record](2026-05-16-digital-houses-e-skills-wearetech). Both figures are the programme's own.

It is the only instrument on this ledger addressed to the interior. The domestic fibre programme has reached the interior one facility at a time - a regional hospital, then a school, sub-prefecture and clinic - and no rural coverage, penetration or affordability figure exists for the country at any date.

summary: The [third statistics development strategy was validated in April 2025 and has no adoption instrument held](2025-04-30-instad-snds3-national-statistics-strategy-lanation).
developments:
The 2025-2029 strategy was [validated at a statistics institute workshop on 29 April 2025 with no adoption instrument held](2025-04-30-instad-snds3-national-statistics-strategy-lanation), and the position is identical at both ends of the window.

Fifteen months from validation to nothing. No adoption decree, budget, indicator set or first publication under it appears on file, and no statistical output of any kind from the institute is held for the window.

summary: [126 years of the legal record were digitised and published online](2026-08-03-djibouti-sgg-pnud-dematerialisation-archives-etat), alongside a standing open-data platform.
developments:
The [open data platform is in service with no dataset inventory or update policy held](2025-06-15-sgdd-a-imf-open-data-national-summary-page-lanation), access arranged through a development bank, and the [national summary data page was launched at the central bank on 12 June 2025 and is published with no update record held](2025-06-15-sgdd-a-imf-open-data-national-summary-page-lanation).

2026-08 - [126 years of the legal record were digitised and published online](2026-08-03-djibouti-sgg-pnud-dematerialisation-archives-etat). The account gives no date for when publication began, so the position at the start of the period cannot be stated. It is the one substantial publication of state information the window records, and it is a legal archive rather than a dataset.

summary: An [industrial and artificial-intelligence cooperation roadmap was presented in Beijing in June 2026](2026-06-22-djibouti-china-industrial-ai-roadmap-beijing-adi), with no agreement or figure.
developments:
2026-06 - a roadmap was [presented to Chinese counterparts and an export-import bank in Beijing, with no agreement, instrument or figure](2026-06-22-djibouti-china-industrial-ai-roadmap-beijing-adi).

The standing commitment is a [grant for an urban security monitoring system, committed and with no implementation record held](2017-01-01-china-mofcom-dji-001-chinese-government-provides-20-million-usd); its own title and its deal field state different amounts and the two have not been reconciled.

The relationship is otherwise visible through delivery rather than instruments: the weather early-warning system in service and the compute memorandum signed in July 2026 both run through Chinese counterparties, and neither is recorded as a bilateral agreement.

summary: [No Gulf-state digital investment or cooperation instrument, figure or programme is held](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority).
developments:
The position is unchanged at both ends of the window: [ties strengthened with one Gulf state in November 2024 are mentioned in passing in a single source, and no instrument, figure or programme is held](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority).

It is a cited absence rather than an unexamined one. In a country whose whole external digital finance runs through three development lenders and one Chinese grant, and whose largest announced project is a memorandum with a Chinese promoter, the absence of Gulf engagement is a fact about the country's partners rather than about the base.

progress: No change, an update to the Smart Nation strategy initiated but not adopted
summary: The [national ICT development policy is still the framework the ministry cites](2025-07-11-mcpt-djibouti-smsi-2025-vision-numerique-inclusif), with no adopted successor on file.
developments:
At a world summit in July 2025 the communications minister [based his account of national progress on the Politique Nationale de Developpement des TIC as the reference framework](2025-07-11-mcpt-djibouti-smsi-2025-vision-numerique-inclusif), naming broadband deployment and two donor projects as its delivery vehicles.

2026-02 - a World Bank supervision report records a [decision to begin updating the Smart Nation strategy to align it with the new national development plan and the new cybersecurity agency](2026-02-10-worldbank-isr8-djibouti-digital-foundations-project).

The ministry's own October 2025 stocktake [still lists a national digital strategy and sectoral roadmaps among the things to be elaborated](2025-10-07-presidence-conseil-ministres-mdeni-catalogue-services-numeriques-diagnostic). Neither policy text is held here, so what either contains is not established.

summary: A [broadband strategy is in place](2024-10-17-lanation-snhd-strategie-nationale-haut-debit) and the [universal service fund it names reached draft decree in April 2026](2026-04-23-armd-universal-service-fund-feedback).
developments:
The [Strategie Nationale du Haut-Debit was unveiled in 2024](2024-10-17-lanation-snhd-strategie-nationale-haut-debit), aligned to Vision 2035 and weighing two coverage scenarios - seven or ten towns by 2027 - with the north served by radio links against optical backbones in the south. No enacting decree for it is held.

2026-04-20 - a regulator and ministry meeting on a World Bank mission's final report [produced a draft decree, an internal bylaw and an operations guide for a Universal Service Fund](2026-04-23-armd-universal-service-fund-feedback), the financing mechanism the strategy names for underserved areas. The fund itself is not yet constituted.

summary: A [sovereign cloud project is envisaged](2024-05-15-worldbank-djibouti-digital-economy-diagnostic) and the ministry [still lists cloud adoption among the tasks outstanding](2025-10-07-presidence-conseil-ministres-mdeni-catalogue-services-numeriques-diagnostic).
developments:
The [Smart Nation roadmap envisages a sovereign cloud project whose implementation begins by defining a national cloud framework](2024-05-15-worldbank-djibouti-digital-economy-diagnostic), a planned instrument rather than an adopted strategy; the same assessment records a central government data centre in operation while many public entities remain on separate infrastructure.

2025-10-07 - the digital economy ministry's report to the Council of Ministers [names modernising infrastructure and promoting cloud adoption among the challenges still to be addressed](2025-10-07-presidence-conseil-ministres-mdeni-catalogue-services-numeriques-diagnostic), seven weeks after the Digital Code was published.

No cloud framework, data-classification rule or public-sector hosting policy is held.

summary: An [interoperability framework is published and maintained by the state information-systems agency](2022-01-01-cadre-interoperabilite-djibouti-cid), with no evidence of application on file.
developments:
The Cadre d'Interoperabilite de Djibouti [sets twelve principles, four interoperability layers - legal, organisational, semantic and technical - and a conceptual model for integrated public-service delivery, with the state information-systems agency designated to maintain it](2022-01-01-cadre-interoperabilite-djibouti-cid).

Nothing dated in the period touches it. The ministry's own service inventory [found the administration fragmented and unevenly equipped, with 503 public services catalogued and 83 selected for digitalisation](2025-10-07-presidence-conseil-ministres-mdeni-catalogue-services-numeriques-diagnostic), which is the closest thing on file to a roadmap and does not reference the framework.

No adoption instrument, compliance record or implementation schedule for the framework is held.

summary: The [Digital Code’s transfer rules came into force in September 2025](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique), regulating international transfers rather than requiring domestic storage.
developments:
Nothing was in force at the period's opening. The Digital Code was [published in the Official Journal on 18 September 2025, its articles 99 to 103 controlling international personal-data transfers through adequacy findings and authorisations rather than a blanket domestic-storage requirement](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique).

No implementing decree, adequacy list or authorisation decision under those articles is held, and the [data-protection commission the Code provides for has no constituting decree on record](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law) - so the body that would operate the regime is not evidenced.

summary: The [Digital Code’s first book is the nearest thing to a national data-governance instrument](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique); no separate policy document exists.
developments:
At the period's opening no data-governance instrument was in force. [Book I of the Digital Code, published on 18 September 2025, carries the personal-data regime](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique) and is the closest instrument on file; no standalone policy document accompanies it.

2025-10-07 - the digital economy ministry [names putting data-management and cybersecurity policies in place among the tasks still outstanding](2025-10-07-presidence-conseil-ministres-mdeni-catalogue-services-numeriques-diagnostic), its own account of what the Code does not supply.

Classification, retention and stewardship rules for state-held data are not held, and neither is any record of the [regime operating](2025-11-05 Review of Djibouti Data Protection Law).

summary: The [Digital Code opened access to administrative documents and the reuse of public data](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique) in September 2025, with an annual catalogue duty.
developments:
No statutory basis for open data was in force at the period's opening. Title 2 of the Digital Code [establishes access to administrative documents and the reuse of public data, and requires an annual government catalogue of what is reusable](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique).

The [national summary data page under the monetary fund's data standard was already in service](2025-06-15-sgdd-a-imf-open-data-national-summary-page-lanation) at both ends of the period.

No catalogue has been published under the new duty on any date on file, and no dataset inventory or update policy for the existing platform is held.

summary: The [Digital Code was published in September 2025](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique) and a [statutory cybersecurity authority followed in December](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority).
developments:
The Digital Code, [regulating personal data, electronic communications, cybersecurity and cybercrime, was published in the Official Journal on 18 September 2025](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique) after adoption on 30 June.

2025-11-04 - the Council of Ministers [approved the bill creating a National Cybersecurity Authority attached to the Presidency, tasked with the national strategy, protection of critical infrastructure and state information systems](2025-11-04-djibouti-presidence-conseil-ministres-anc-bill); the [National Assembly passed it on 12 November](2025-11-12 Djibouti advances bill to create National Cybersecurity Authority).

A World Bank report records [operationalising the Code's telecommunications and cybersecurity books as a priority](2026-02-10-worldbank-isr8-djibouti-digital-foundations-project); no implementing decree under either is held.

summary: Identification is governed by a [2019 law creating the register of natural persons and the national identification number](2019-01-21-djibouti-loi-39-an-19-rnpp), unchanged in the period.
developments:
The founding law [makes the Registre National des Personnes Physiques the unique reference for identifying individuals and for producing every secure national document - identity card, passport, voter card, driving licence - with administrative management at the population directorate and technical and security management at the state information-systems agency](2019-01-21-djibouti-loi-39-an-19-rnpp).

Its [implementing decree defines the identification number as a digital instrument combining civil-status and personal data, and makes its use compulsory across public, parapublic and private administration for identification and third-party data exchange](2020-07-13-decret-2020-150-nni-composition-caracteristiques).

Nothing amended either in the period; what moved is what runs on them.

summary: Payments are governed by a [2016 law placing every payment service under central-bank licensing and supervision](2016-07-16-djibouti-loi-118-systeme-paiement-national), unchanged in the period.
developments:
The law [applies to every payment service and system operated in the country, empowers the central bank to license, regulate and supervise payment-system providers, and defines electronic money and electronic funds transfer](2016-07-16-djibouti-loi-118-systeme-paiement-national).

Beneath it the central bank acts by instruction rather than by statute: from [31 August 2025 all cheques had to meet new format, security and encoding standards, with non-conforming cheques refused by the settlement platform and legacy stock withdrawn](2025-07-07-djibouti-bcd-communique-syrad-normes-cheques), a measure that took effect a day before this period opened.

No amendment, and no implementing text on electronic money issued in the period, is held.

summary: A [2022 law gives the digital economy ministry a statutory mandate over the interoperability of state information systems](2022-07-27-djibouti-loi-164-mdeni-missions), unchanged in the period.
developments:
The law establishing the ministry [charges it with ensuring the coherence and interoperability of information systems by design, breaking down ministerial application silos and enabling data sharing between administrations through a dedicated platform](2022-07-27-djibouti-loi-164-mdeni-missions), in force since 27 July 2022.

It is a mandate on a ministry rather than a duty on data holders: no law compels an administration to expose its data, and no implementing decree under this article is held. The [interoperability framework the state information-systems agency maintains](2022-01-01-cadre-interoperabilite-djibouti-cid) is a technical document with no enacting instrument on file.

summary: Two decrees and an order in the period [created a specialised statistical corps](2026-05-12-journalofficiel-decret-2026-075-statut-cadres-instad) and [approved the institute’s 2026 budget](2026-02-25-djibouti-arrete-2026-041-budget-instad).
developments:
2026-02-25 - the institute's [2026 forecast budget of 485,686,344 FDJ was approved by order, following board adoption on 18 November 2025 and Council of Ministers review on 23 December](2026-02-25-djibouti-arrete-2026-041-budget-instad).

2026-05-12 - a decree [created a specialised civil-service corps of statisticians, engineers, senior administrators and technicians, charged with compiling, analysing and projecting socio-demographic, economic and environmental data](2026-05-12-journalofficiel-decret-2026-075-statut-cadres-instad).

2026-06-11 - a government reorganisation decree [assigns the finance ministry responsibility for the national strategy on collecting, processing and disseminating official statistics](2026-06-11-journalofficiel-decret-2026-105-attributions-ministeres).

No founding statistics law is held; these are instruments made under a framework the base does not carry.

summary: [No access-to-information law exists](2026-04-01-djibouti-statemediamonitor-country-panel); the 1992 law on freedom of communication is the only instrument on the field.
developments:
This is a searched absence rather than an unexamined one. A [country panel dated April 2026 records that the media and information regime is still governed solely by the law of 15 September 1992 on freedom of communication, never substantially reformed in more than three decades, with no dedicated access-to-information instrument](2026-04-01-djibouti-statemediamonitor-country-panel).

The same panel names the communication regulator as the operative body and [places the country 167th of 180 on the 2026 press-freedom index](2026-04-01-djibouti-statemediamonitor-country-panel).

The Digital Code's [own title on access to administrative documents](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique) is the nearest statutory route, and it is a reuse provision rather than a right of access with a procedure.

summary: The country [hosted a continental private-sector forum that adopted a Djibouti Declaration on digital trade](2025-12-11-au-16th-psf-djibouti-declaration) in December 2025.
developments:
2025-10-06 - a [three-day regional consultation in Arta on an information sharing and analysis centre](2025-10-06-igad-cyber-resilience-workshop-djibouti) advanced a regional cyber-threat mechanism aligned to the continental convention.

2025-12-08 - the [16th African Union Private Sector Forum, held in Djibouti, adopted the Djibouti Declaration on digital-trade implementation, data-protection and cybersecurity alignment, digital public infrastructure and interoperable payments](2025-12-11-au-16th-psf-djibouti-declaration).

2026-06 - senior policymakers [joined a regional data-governance workshop in Nairobi drafting harmonised regional data-policy roadmaps](2026-07-21-unesco-east-africa-data-governance-workshop-nairobi).

Standing behind these, the [regional health data-sharing framework of 2022](2022-06-16-igad-regional-health-data-sharing-framework) is non-binding and its domestication is not evidenced complete.

summary: A [tripartite agreement for a terrestrial fibre corridor to Ethiopia and Sudan was signed on 4 February 2026](2026-02-04-ethiotelecom-horizon-fiber-tripartite-signing).
developments:
2025-08-28 - the national operator [announced a southward extension of its regional express cable from Mombasa to Durban, with new landings in Tanzania, Mozambique, Madagascar and South Africa, service-ready 2028](2025-08-28-dare1-subsea-cable-extension).

2026-02-04 - the [Ethiopian, Djiboutian and Sudanese operators signed a tripartite agreement for the Horizon Fiber corridor, a terrestrial multi-terabit route connecting the Djiboutian and Sudanese landing stations through Ethiopia](2026-02-04-ethiotelecom-horizon-fiber-tripartite-signing), building on a December 2024 memorandum.

The operator's own account puts [13 submarine cable systems, ten of them operational, reaching 90 countries](2024-07-17-djibouti-telecom-connectivity-hub). Neither new route carries a stated capacity price or access condition for neighbouring states on file.

summary: [Transfer rules entered force with the Digital Code in September 2025](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique) and a regional pilot mechanism is [under preparation](2025-09-12-worldbank-eardip-implementation-mission-aide-memoire).
developments:
The Digital Code's [articles 99 to 103 control international personal-data transfers by adequacy finding or authorisation](2025-09-18-djibouti-loi-019-code-numerique), in force from 18 September 2025 where nothing stood before.

2025-09 - a regional integration project mission records the [July 2025 ministerial call for the two regional bodies to pilot a trusted cross-border personal-data-flow mechanism within twelve months](2025-09-12-worldbank-eardip-implementation-mission-aide-memoire), with a technical working group on data protection and cross-border data.

No adequacy finding, authorisation or transfer decision has been published, and the [regional health data-sharing framework remains non-binding](2022-06-16-igad-regional-health-data-sharing-framework).

summary: The [national interoperability framework sets the standards layer](2022-01-01-cadre-interoperabilite-djibouti-cid); no technical specification or conformance register is held.
developments:
The framework [defines a technical interoperability layer and a semantic layer, and provides for governance-level standards and specifications maintained by the state information-systems agency](2022-01-01-cadre-interoperabilite-djibouti-cid).

What is not on file is the layer below it: no published technical specification, data-exchange schema, application-programming interface catalogue or conformance register.

The one system in the period described as exchanging data to a stated pattern is the [national mobile identity service, where partner administrations query authentication server-to-server without direct access to the biometric database](2026-02-10-interieur-mobile-id-lancement-officiel) - an architecture stated by its owner rather than a published standard.

summary: The standards agency [operationalised two technical standardisation committees in 2025](2026-01-13-conseil-ministres-adn-budget-ctn-operationalises), its first sectoral standards capacity on file.
developments:
The agency is the [national reference body for standardisation, metrology, certification, accreditation and quality promotion, organised by decree in 2022](2022-05-04-decret-2022-092-pr-mct-adn-organisation).

2026-01-13 - the Council of Ministers records that [two technical standardisation committees, for agri-food and for electrical and household products, were operationalised during 2025, and approves a 2026 budget of 134.9 million FDJ against 112.1 million in 2025, including 54.4 million of investment for laboratory equipment, software and instrumentation](2026-01-13-conseil-ministres-adn-budget-ctn-operationalises).

The agency's two founding laws are not held, and no standard published by the committees appears on file.

summary: [Risk-management training on an international security standard was delivered to government and critical-infrastructure staff in December 2025](2025-12-16-itu-iso-27005-training-djibouti).
developments:
2025-12-16 - the telecommunications union's regional office [delivered three days of ISO/IEC 27005 risk-manager training in Djibouti for government, critical-infrastructure and ICT-sector participants](2025-12-16-itu-iso-27005-training-djibouti), covering risk context-setting, identification and evaluation.

The route by which a standard becomes binding runs through the standards agency, whose [technical committees homologate standards by sector and began operating in 2025](2026-01-13-conseil-ministres-adn-budget-ctn-operationalises).

No adopted international standard is named in any instrument on file, and no certification or accreditation issued against one appears in the record.

summary: Four dated consultations in the period took [non-government participants into policy formation](2026-01-30-unesco-djibouti-strategie-nationale-ia-consultation), from the development plan to the AI strategy.
developments:
2025-08-06 - a [regional consultation at Dikhil for the third national development plan brought elected officials, local authorities, civil society and experts into the plan's formulation, each region required to produce a validated contribution report](2025-08-10-lanation-pnd-2025-2030-consultations-dikhil).

2025-10-06 - [co-design workshops with producers, extension agents, community radios, associations and private-sector actors produced an editorial and data-governance framework for digital agricultural advisory services](2025-10-07-brefons-codesign-workshop-digital-agriculture-djibouti).

2025-12-06 - a [validation workshop at Tadjourah reviewed the draft national land policy with ministries, regional authorities and national institutions](2025-12-07-igad-validation-workshop-politique-fonciere-nationale).

2026-01-22 - a national AI-strategy workshop of [about eighty participants included academia alongside government, the United Nations, the private sector and civil society](2026-01-30-unesco-djibouti-strategie-nationale-ia-consultation).

summary: The [President publicly set out the risks of the national digital identity system](2026-02-09-presidence-discours-forum-identite-numerique), and the Digital Code was discussed outside government.
developments:
2025-11-06 - the ministry [presented the newly adopted Digital Code to a France-Djibouti business assembly, its legal adviser setting out the personal-data and electronic-commerce provisions](2025-11-06-techreviewafrica-djibouti-digital-code-gafd-general-assembly).

2026-02-09 - closing the national digital identity forum, the [President addressed identity theft, cloning, hacking, espionage and over-centralisation alongside the benefits, and called for continuing public vigilance](2026-02-09-presidence-discours-forum-identite-numerique).

The setting bounds what this shows. A country panel dated April 2026 [records the 1992 communication law as never substantially reformed and places the country 167th of 180 on the press-freedom index](2026-04-01-djibouti-statemediamonitor-country-panel); the discussion on file is government-convened.

summary: A [tripartite fibre agreement with the Ethiopian and Sudanese operators was signed in February 2026](2026-02-04-ethiotelecom-horizon-fiber-tripartite-signing); no sum is stated in it.
developments:
The standing relationship on file is with a platform foundation: a [memorandum signed on 9 December 2024 to deploy an open-source service platform, including a construction-permit system, with capacity-building and knowledge transfer](2024-12-09-egov-mdeni-mou-digital-transformation).

2025-09-21 - an [Ethiopian payments operator and a Djiboutian financial-services provider signed a partnership on cross-border payments, remittances and merchant services, witnessed by four ministers](2025-09-21-santimpay-meras-djibouti-partnership).

2026-02-04 - the [three national operators signed the tripartite Horizon Fiber agreement](2026-02-04-ethiotelecom-horizon-fiber-tripartite-signing).

None of the three states a committed amount, so what any of them is worth is not established here.
